TL;DR: Glass cannon wizard simulator roguelike

This game is as fun as it is punishing - building wands, the procedural environments, and the sheer variety of possible deaths keeps me coming back for more runs. You can die thousands of ways, and also build spells that do literal millions of damage out of 5 damage projectiles.

If you get frustrated easily, avoid this game. It is simultaneously one of the best games of the last 10 years, and unbelievably punishing (including RNG wise) towards the player. You WILL lose hours of progress on a god-run to an enemy that polymorphs you into a sheep, or a misclick on an explosive - but it makes achieving the variety of wins and objectives hidden within the game all the more satisfying.

The sheer quanitity of secrets, the lore, the alchemy portion of the game, the very spell mechanics, it holds your hand on none of it. There is so much hidden beneath the surface, and it is SO GOOD.

this is an amazing game, once you actually play it enough to learn how to play it becomes more of a fight against RNG if anything. Noita is a game about community.

It's esoteric story/world building, dark caves, and endless enemies can make things quite challenging. Yet more and more I see new players finding their path, and it's all thanks to them.

The wiki, discord, and videos found across the internet is your Grimoire.
You merely need to study and decipher it.

Without the years of players ripping the files, the countless failures in trial by fire, and great people you will meet along the way; this game would be near impossible, but not entirely.

Consider playing this game without spoilers the real challenge, but not one most should attempt.
For becoming a learned alchemist on their own is a task that even fewer have achieved.
Not without plenty of mods to make their goals obtuse.

The first few times I played this, I was of the opinion it was too hard. This is as an avid player of roguelike games for a number of years. After the last update, and discovering mod access, I can say this is one of the games I've most enjoyed playing in the last couple years. It reminds me a lot of the Magic Makers game where you create your own spells, and I love the chaos of the particle physics and randomly getting gutted by an unlikely backfiring of your own spells.

The thing that would put this over the top for me is if there was a way to customize your own preferred starting class without resorting to modding capabilities. I like having the extra time to collect gold, the extra items, and the random but always welcome super anvil, but sometimes you really want credit where credit is due.

About as "true roguelike" as a game can come. With the exception of a few spells unlocked by defeating secret bosses , The only thing you keep between games is your own knowledge of the Noita's mechanics. The game is hard, and you'll die a lot, but you learn from each one. It won't teach you anything outright because you're expected to learn by experimenting. A tablet you can find in-game reads, "The sacrifice of oneself to the pursuit of knowledge is the highest tribute to the gods."

Rarely will a death be the result of the game being unfair- you're the one to blame 99% of the time. And so you learn that you should always carry water in case you get set on fire or covered in toxic sludge, or you learn to not fire off wands without checking what spells they carry.

Tinkering with wands between levels is where the game's true complexity shines. Good things happen when you add a chainsaw and multicast to a wand with a trigger spell that creates explosions at its impact point.

Noita may give you it's toughest battles, but you are it's strongest alchemist. And remember- True Knowledge is not offered for free.

At around 230 hrs of gameplay I gained two surprising insights: 1. mysteriously and withdrawn from my consciousness this game has become my number one most played game ever (including every console, system, platform). 2. at that time I got an achievement "The Gods are impressed" and despite the playing time I had to stop the game and google what the hell triggered this achievement (while I was hapharzardly fiddling with wands in a holy mountain) - that's when I understood that despite the game time I might have only scratched the surface by then. If you were ever looking for proof that chaos theory and determinism don't contradict each other, if you like (advanced)pixel-art, or - to quote a friend: if just want to get a max amount of pain for a really low price: give this game a go. It's one of a kind.

Despite looking significantly more approachable, this game is much harder than Baba is You. Nothing is explained, and every little thing you learn about the world comes at the end of a 15+ minute run. I'm amazed they were able to fit this volume of content into a game, it makes pretty much every other game look half-finished.

This game is not for the faint of heart or the easily discouraged. It punishes you for all the things you dont know or can't predict. The game physics interactions are convoluted, the spell building is incredibly complex in the late game, and almost none of the game's secret's are straightforward. However; if you like the feeling of that 1 success in 500 when you start out, and enjoy trying to navigate a maze of threats seemingly designed to prevent survival, then you might find this to be a rewarding challenge. Personally, I occasionally crave this level of difficulty in a sea of spoon-feeding, dopamine flooding, micro-transactions disguised as 'games'.

I was playing, and then... I noticed the sun went down... I decided to play 1 more, and the sun rose... I got breakfast, decided to play 1 more, and then collapsed from exhaustion... and I still do not know, how this game is not a certified time machine.

tldr.text: Overwhelmingly Positive (96%): players praise the gameplay and combat most often.
The main complaint is bugs and crashes, though only a small share of reviews mention them.

details.text: Bug complaints have become less common lately, with a smaller share of recent reviews raising bugs and crashes than across all reviews.
Newer players are less enthusiastic, with 77% of those under 2 hours positive, against 97% of those over 50 hours.
